source_of_truth: The Visual Operating Console roadmap shipped a local operator dashboard for one active repo. This follow-on makes the same local dashboard usable across many registered repos/apps/platforms while preserving the command-emitter and no-mutation invariant.

user_journeys.name: operator-with-three-projects-opens-all-projects-dashboard
user_journeys.description: An operator who has registered DontPanic, an app repo, and a backend repo opens the dashboard and sees All Projects as the default with grouped What Now actions and warning counts by project.
acceptance_signals: Fleet summary lists all registered project names and display names
Project selector defaults to All Projects when multiple projects exist
What Now groups actions by project
Status header identifies Fleet scope and warning counts

user_journeys.name: operator-selects-one-project-and-sees-scoped-state
user_journeys.description: An operator selects one project from the dashboard selector and sees What Now and Status scoped to that project, with only relevant global blockers included.
acceptance_signals: Selected project survives reload through local browser state
Project view excludes unrelated project actions
Relevant global capability or install blockers still render
Visible sections declare Scope: Project or Scope: Global

user_journeys.name: agent-reads-fleet-summary-without-scraping-html
user_journeys.description: An agent reads the fleet summary and project cache files to summarize which repo needs human work, without parsing the dashboard UI.
acceptance_signals: Fleet summary contains schema_version, project names, health bands, warning counts, and cache paths
Per-project what-now cache contains project_name fields
Cache files do not contain secret values
JSON shape is covered by snapshot or schema-style tests

user_journeys.name: operator-in-unregistered-single-repo-gets-current-behavior
user_journeys.description: A user who installs DontPanic and runs the dashboard from one unregistered repo still gets a useful current-repo dashboard without first configuring a project registry.
acceptance_signals: Dashboard serve/build works when ~/.dontpanic/projects.json is absent
Selector does not force registration for single-repo use
The UI shows how to register the repo for future multi-project use
Doctor/init do not treat missing project registry as an error

user_journeys.name: operator-sees-malformed-project-warning-in-dashboard
user_journeys.description: A project with a malformed plan or skipped state source no longer hides the problem in terminal output only; the dashboard Status and All Projects view show an actionable warning.
acceptance_signals: Build warning JSON persists skipped/malformed source details without secrets
Status header warning count increments
All Projects groups the warning under the affected project
The visible remediation includes an exact command when available

non_goals: No dashboard mutation of project registry or plan state
No hosted dashboard or control plane
No generated dashboard files written into target repos by default
No secret values in cache, warnings, or UI
completion_test: With two fixture projects and the DontPanic repo registered, `dontpanic dashboard serve` defaults to All Projects unless cwd matches a registered project, renders a project selector, groups What Now actions by project, shows Fleet-scope Status with warning counts, and writes agent-readable fleet/project JSON caches. Selecting one project filters What Now and Status to that project while preserving relevant global blockers. An 8-project synthetic fleet exercises grouping and sorting. Running without a project registry still serves the current-repo dashboard. Firebase is not required and the dashboard does not mutate state.
